issues.detail: Example vector {x:0,y:3} expects Y0=1, but spec row 011 x=0 gives next state 001 so Y0=1; however {x:1,y:3} expects Y0=0 but spec row 011 x=1 gives next state 010 so Y0=0. Wait, check {x:0,y:0}: spec 000 x=0 -> 000 Y0=0 ok; {x:1,y:0}: 000 x=1 -> 001 Y0=1 ok. Actually examples match spec. No issue? Re-evaluate: R_Y0 example vectors: (0,0)->Y0=0,z=0; (1,0)->Y0=1,z=0; (0,3)->Y0=1,z=1; (1,3)->Y0=0,z=1. Spec: y=3 (011): x=0 -> 001 Y0=1 z=1; x=1 -> 010 Y0=0 z=1. All match. So no consistency issue here.
R_z example vector {x:1,y:4} expects Y0=0,z=1. Spec row 100: x=1 -> next state 100, Y0=0, z=1. Matches. {x:0,y:2} expects Y0=0,z=0; spec 010 x=0 -> 010 Y0=0 z=0. Matches. No issue.
Spec does not define behavior for present state y=101,110,111. Contract rules give no condition for these states; outputs undefined.
issues.alternative: Treat undefined states as don't-cares: Y0=0,z=0 for y=101,110,111.
